causes.label: You forgot to enter a bake temperature or cleaning time.
remedies: Press the BAKE pad and desired temperature or the SELF CLEAN pad and desired clean time.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "You forgot to enter a bake temperature or cleaning time."

causes.label: Incorrect cookware or cookware of improper size being used.

remedies: See the Broiling Guide.

causes.label: Food being cooked in a hot pan.
remedies: Use the broiling pan and grid that came with your oven.
Make sure it is cool.

causes.label: Cookware not suited for broiling.

causes.label: In some areas the power (voltage) may be low.

Broil for the longest period of time recommended in the Broiling Guide.

causes.label: Light bulb is loose or defective.
remedies: Tighten or replace the bulb.

causes.label: Pad operating light is broken.
remedies: Call for service.

symptoms.symptom: Oven temperature too hot or too cold

causes.label: Oven thermostat needs adjustment.
remedies: See the Adjust the oven thermostat—Do it yourself! section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Oven thermostat needs adjustment."

causes.label: A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped.
remedies: Replace the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped."

causes.label: Oven controls improperly set.
remedies: See the Using the oven section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Oven controls improperly set."

causes.label: The oven temperature is too high to set a self-clean operation.
remedies: Allow the oven to cool to room temperature and reset the controls.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "The oven temperature is too high to set a self-clean operation."

causes.label: Oven controls improperly set.
remedies: See the Using the self-cleaning oven section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Oven controls improperly set."

causes.label: This is the sound of the metal heating and cooling during both the cooking and cleaning functions.
remedies: This is normal.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "This is the sound of the metal heating and cooling during both the cooking and cleaning functions."

causes.label: Excessive soil.
remedies: Press the CLEAR/OFF pad.
Open the windows to rid the room of smoke.
Wait until the LOCKED DOOR light goes off.
Wipe up the excess soil and reset the clean cycle.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Excessive soil."

symptoms.symptom: Oven door will not open after a clean cycle

causes.label: Oven too hot.
remedies: Allow the oven to cool below locking temperature.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Oven too hot."

symptoms.symptom: Oven not clean after a clean cycle

causes.label: Oven controls improperly set.
remedies: See the Using the self-cleaning oven section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Oven controls improperly set."

causes.label: Oven was heavily soiled.
remedies: Clean up heavy spillovers before starting the clean cycle.
Heavily soiled ovens may need to self-clean again or for a longer period of time.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Oven was heavily soiled."

causes.label: The self-clean cycle has been selected but the door is not closed.
remedies: Close the oven door.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "The self-clean cycle has been selected but the door is not closed."

symptoms.symptom: LOCKED DOOR light is on when you want to cook

causes.label: The oven door is locked because the temperature inside the oven has not dropped below the locking temperature.
remedies: Press the CLEAR/OFF pad.
Allow the oven to cool.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "The oven door is locked because the temperature inside the oven has not dropped below the locking temperature."

symptoms.symptom: “F— and a number or letter” flash in the display

causes.label: You have a function error code.
remedies: Press the CLEAR/OFF pad.
Allow the oven to cool for one hour.
Put the oven back into operation.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "You have a function error code."

causes.label: If the function code repeats.
remedies: Disconnect all power to the oven for at least 30 seconds and then reconnect power.
If the function error code repeats, call for service.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "If the function code repeats."

causes.label: A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped.
remedies: Replace the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped."

causes.label: The clock is in the black-out mode.
remedies: See the Special features of your oven control section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "The clock is in the black-out mode."

causes.label: Power failure.
remedies: Reset the clock.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Power failure."

symptoms.symptom: Unable to get the display to show “SF”

causes.label: Oven control pads were not pressed properly.
remedies: The BAKE and BROIL HI/LO pads must be pressed at the same time and held for 3 seconds.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Oven control pads were not pressed properly."

causes.label: Power outage or surge.
remedies: Reset the clock.
If the oven was in use, you must reset it by pressing the CLEAR/OFF pad, setting the clock and resetting any cooking function.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "Power outage or surge."

symptoms.symptom: “Burning” or “oily” odor emitting from the vent

causes.label: This is normal in a new oven and will disappear in time.
remedies: To speed the process, set a self-clean cycle for a minimum of 3 hours.
See the Using the self-cleaning oven section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "This is normal in a new oven and will disappear in time."

causes.label: An odor from the insulation around the inside of the oven is normal for the first few times the oven is used.
remedies: This is temporary.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "An odor from the insulation around the inside of the oven is normal for the first few times the oven is used."

causes.label: A cooling fan may automatically turn on and off to cool internal parts.
remedies: This is normal.
The cooling fan will turn off and on.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 23: "A cooling fan may automatically turn on and off to cool internal parts."
